title: Quantization run management and access controls for calibration artifacts
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Background: Customers are running automated calibration jobs to generate quantization profiles (FP8/INT8) and accuracy validation artifacts. Today these runs and their outputs are stored with inconsistent retention and limited access controls, causing confusion for platform teams and blocking enterprise customers that require strict artifact governance.

Problem statement: We need a single, opinionated orchestration surface in Redwood Console to manage calibration runs, artifact retention policies, access controls (RBAC), and accuracy validation artifacts so teams can audit, reproduce, and roll back quantization profiles safely.

Goals: Provide UX and API primitives to: 1) Start/stop calibration runs and view run history; 2) Attach per-run metadata (model version, dataset, seed, profile settings); 3) Store artifacts (quant profiles, calibration traces, eval results) with configurable retention tiers; 4) Apply role-based access control for viewing/downloading artifacts and ability to mark artifacts as "canonical" or "archived"; 5) Surface accuracy delta compared to baseline and gate rollouts when regressions exceed thresholds.

Non-goals: This ticket does not cover full CI integration for automated retrain triggers, nor deep storage optimization (those are follow-ups).

Intended users: ML engineers running quantization experiments, platform SREs auditing production rollouts, and security/compliance reviewers needing artifact provenance.
acceptance_criteria: Console: Users can start a calibration run from model detail page and see a streaming status for run progress.
Artifacts: Each run produces a named artifact bundle (quant_profile.json, calibration_trace.pb, eval_report.html) and these are accessible from the run detail page.
Retention: Admins can set org-level and project-level default retention tiers (30d, 90d, indefinite) and override per-run.
RBAC: Console enforces roles so that only users with 'Calibration Viewer' can download artifacts; 'Calibration Admin' can change retention and mark canonical artifacts.
Accuracy gating: Runs compute accuracy deltas vs pinned baseline and flag regressions over the configured threshold in the UI and via webhook.
API: Public API endpoints exist to list runs, fetch artifact URLs, and set retention; responses follow documented schema and return signed URLs for downloads.
Audit log: Every artifact download, retention change, and mark-as-canonical action is recorded in the audit log with user, timestamp, and run id.
proposed_design:
- UI: New 'Calibration runs' tab under Model > Manage. Run row shows status, created_by, profile type (FP8/INT8), accuracy delta, size, artifact retention. Run detail shows artifacts with preview (eval_report) and download button. Admin modal for retention policy.
- API: POST /v1/models/:id/calibration_runs to start. GET /v1/calibration_runs/:id to fetch metadata. GET /v1/calibration_runs/:id/artifacts to list artifact files. POST /v1/calibration_runs/:id/retention to set retention.
- Storage: Artifacts stored in customer-backed bucket for Private deployments or Redwood-managed object store for Hosted; keys namespaced by org/project/model/run_id. Signed URL generation delegated to storage service.
- RBAC: Map roles to existing Console roles via permissions service. Add two new granular permissions: calibration.view_artifacts and calibration.manage_retention.
- Retention model: Three tiers (short=30d, standard=90d, permanent=indefinite) plus ability to pin to permanent. Default is 'standard' for new orgs.
- Accuracy validation: During run, evaluator computes summary metrics and stores eval_report.html. Console computes delta and shows color-coded badge and threshold badge if > configured threshold.
implementation_notes: Backend: Extend run service to emit artifact manifest to metadata DB and to call storage service for signed URL lifecycle.
Storage: Use lifecycle policies for Redwood-managed buckets to implement retention; expose UI to set lifecycle for customer buckets only with proper permissions.
Authz: Integrate with existing RBAC module; ensure audit log events are emitted for all artifact actions.
Telemetry: Add metrics: calibration_runs_started, calibration_runs_failed, artifacts_downloaded, retention_changes, accuracy_regressions_detected.
Data model: Store run metadata fields: run_id, model_id, model_commit, profile_type, dataset_id, seed, started_by, status, accuracy_metrics_summary, artifact_manifest_url.
Migration: Backfill recent calibration runs (last 90 days) to populate artifact manifest for UI listing; coordinated with ENG-2981.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal): Launch to Redwood internal org only. Collect feedback from platform and ML teams for 2 weeks.
Phase 2 (beta): Opt-in for selected hosted customers and all Dedicated customers; monitor artifact storage usage and permission correctness.
Phase 3 (GA): Enabled by default with org-level defaults; provide migration docs and support run-book for enterprise audits.
Feature flags: gate storage changes and RBAC enforcement behind feature flags to allow quick rollback.
test_plan: Unit tests for API endpoints and signed URL generation.
Integration tests for retention lifecycle transitions and artifact availability after simulated expiry.
E2E UI tests for starting runs, viewing artifacts, downloading, and audit log entries.
Security review: penetration test for artifact signed URL access and permission escalation scenarios.
Performance test: measure artifact listing latency for runs with 1k artifacts and evaluate pagination strategy.

notes: Keep artifact filenames stable across runs to make downstream evaluation reproducible. Consider adding a manifest checksum to enable quick integrity checks.
outstanding_risks: Storage cost growth if many orgs set 'permanent' retention without quota controls.
Signed URL leak risk if long-lived URLs are issued; mitigate by short TTL and token refresh.
Compatibility differences between Redwood-managed and customer buckets could complicate lifecycle enforcement.
